questions.q: Name two physical properties that distinguish most non-metals from metals.
questions.a: Non-metals are generally dull (lack lustre) and are poor conductors of heat and electricity. A student who says "non-metals are hard and shiny" is likely confusing them with metals, revealing they have not yet grasped the basic appearance difference.

questions.q: Why is plastic used to coat the metal wires in your house?
questions.a: Plastic is a non-metal that acts as an insulator, meaning it does not allow electricity to pass through it, protecting us from shocks. A student who says "because it is pretty" misses the functional scientific property of conductivity.

questions.q: If you have a piece of sulfur and a piece of iron, how can you test which one is a metal?
questions.a: First, observe if it is shiny (lustre); then, try to see if it conducts heat or electricity. Metals are shiny and conduct; sulfur is dull and does not conduct. This shows the student can apply the definition to a practical test.

questions.q: Are all non-lustrous materials necessarily non-metals?
questions.a: No, some metals can appear dull due to oxidation or weathering, and some materials like wood are non-metals but are not shiny. A student who says "yes" assumes that appearance is the only factor, ignoring surface changes or material types.

questions.q: Could you use a non-metal like rubber to make a cooking pot? Why or why not?
questions.a: No, because rubber is a poor conductor of heat and would melt or burn before cooking the food, unlike metal which transfers heat efficiently. If a student says "yes," they fail to understand the property of thermal conductivity required for kitchenware.

questions.q: Think of three non-metals you interact with daily and describe how their property of being a non-metal makes them useful.
questions.a: Examples: Oxygen (gas state, needed for breathing), Plastic (insulator, for electrical safety), and Cotton/Fabric (soft, for clothing). A poor answer fails to connect the property to the specific use.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Non-metals are materials that generally lack metallic properties such as lustre, ______, and the ability to conduct heat or electricity.
Fill in the blank: Have you ever wondered why the handle of a pressure cooker is made of ______ while the body is metal?
What is Non-metals? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Non-metals are materials that generally lack metallic properties such as lustre, malleability, and the ability to conduct heat or electricity.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Non-metals?
questions.a: Students often believe that if a material is solid and hard, it must be a metal.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to classify a given material as a non-metal based on its physical properties (appearance, conductivity, and state) and distinguish it from metals through simple observation.
